title: Apartment Design 75 m² in Bratislava, Metropolis
description: 75 m² apartment (Metropolis) in Bratislava: interior design (“Furniture” package), 3D visualization and custom furniture.
h1: Apartment interior design in Metropolis, Bratislava, custom furniture, 75 m²

blocks.text: Apartment interior design in Metropolis, Bratislava, custom furniture, 75 m²

parts.html: A 75 m² apartment in the Metropolis residential complex in central Bratislava. The owners received it from the developer with a basic finish. We did the project under the “Furniture” design package: the interior concept, 3D visualizations and technical documentation, and we designed the built-in furniture and made it in our own workshop in Bratislava. Upholstered furniture, lighting and decor were selected to suit the design. Solutions and materials were chosen to fit the client’s budget, and the project was carried out with design supervision.

The largest room is the kitchen-living room, with a dining area by the window and a sofa in the middle. A corridor leads from the entrance hall past the bedroom, the bathroom and a separate laundry room. The second room is a home office with a sofa that can later be turned into a child’s room.

The kitchen runs in a single line along the wall. At each end is a floor-to-ceiling oak-effect column, the left one housing the oven and microwave, and in between are light matte handleless fronts and a light stone-effect backsplash. Above the kitchen is a black track with spotlights, and a linear pendant hangs over the dining table. Opposite the sofa is a wall of light panels with fine joints and a long wall-mounted oak-effect unit for the TV and electronics.

In the bedroom a wardrobe in dark walnut-effect veneer runs along the wall from the door to the window, and there is a wall-mounted console by the window. In the study a graphite desk stands end-on to the wall, with a sofa next to it. The wall behind them is finished with wood-effect panels and dark slats, and tall cabinets with a niche and a shelf line the other wall.

The entrance hall has a floor-to-ceiling wardrobe and, next to it, a niche with an upholstered seat, hooks and shoe space below. Opposite are mirrored doors. In the bathroom the walls and floor are covered in large white marble-effect tiles with gray veining, with a wall-hung wood-effect vanity with a white countertop and a lit mirror cabinet.

Further down the page is a sample of the technical documentation for the “Furniture” package, starting with the measured floor plan, a 3D view of the apartment and photos of the site before work began.
